paragraphs: Here's my big idea, friend: God is the One who meets with His people, and He is the One who decides how. He says the gold altar goes before the veil, "where I will meet with you" (Exodus 30:6). The incense, the ransom, the washing and the oil all come from Him, and none of it is Moses' idea. I once "improved" a recipe nobody asked me to improve, and the cookies let me know about it LOUDLY.

Coming near to God is serious, and this passage doesn't whisper it. Aaron and his sons wash "so that they will not die" (Exodus 30:20). But nobody gets a VIP line, either. Every counted man pays the same half shekel, because "the rich shall not give more than a half shekel, nor shall the poor give less" (Exodus 30:15).

The holy things also aren't for us to borrow for our own enjoyment. God says anyone who makes incense like His "to enjoy its fragrance shall be cut off from his people" (Exodus 30:38). So when you open the Word, friend, come the way He has made, with respect and with a glad heart, because He's the One who invited you. And hold on, because the teaching isn't over, and the LORD still has more to say.
